climex

English | Español

Climate data of Mexico from the NASA POWER API: daily, monthly or climatological temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind and radiation for the 2,465 municipalities of Mexico or any set of points. It is part of the dengueverse; the Python version is climex-py.

Installation 

install.packages("climex", repos = c("https://fdzul.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

Usage 

library(climex)

yuc <- municipalities("31")          # the 106 municipalities of Yucatán; municipalities() = all the country
clima <- download_nasa_power_data(
    yuc, id_col = "CVEGEO",
    parameters = c("T2M", "T2M_MAX", "T2M_MIN", "PRECTOTCORR", "RH2M"),
    start_date = "20240101", end_date = "20241231",
    temporal_resolution = "daily", community = "AG")

The result has one row per municipality and day (identifier, latitude, longitude, date and one column per parameter), only for the period requested and without duplicates. Each point is saved as a CSV in output_folder, so a download that stops can be run again and continues where it stopped; with a later end_date (a weekly update) only the new period is asked again.

Documentation: https://fdzul.github.io/climex/

Español

Datos climáticos de México de la API de NASA POWER: temperatura, precipitación, humedad, viento y radiación diarios, mensuales o climatológicos para los 2,465 municipios de México o cualquier conjunto de puntos. Es parte del dengueverse; la versión en Python es climex-py.

library(climex)
yuc <- municipalities("31")          # municipios de Yucatán; municipalities() = todo el país
clima <- download_nasa_power_data(yuc, id_col = "CVEGEO",
                                  parameters = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"),
                                  start_date = "20240101", end_date = "20241231")

El resultado tiene una fila por municipio y día, solo del periodo pedido y sin duplicados. Si la descarga se interrumpe, se vuelve a correr y continúa donde se quedó.
